request.style: English, male baritone, warm and steady, solo voice with gentle backing choir, acoustic guitar, cello, harp, soft percussion, 80 BPM, solemn and narrative
request.lyrics:
[Verse]
From Gerar the king rides out to the field
With Phicol, the commander, standing by
He speaks to the patriarch, voice low and mild
God is with you in everything you do, he said
Swear to me here by the God of high heaven
That you will not deal falsely with my line
I will show you kindness, as you have shown me
In the land where you have stayed as a stranger

[Chorus]
Phicol the commander of the army stands
Witness to the oath, the covenant in hands
Seven ewe lambs set apart from the flock
Accept these as my witness that I dug this well

[Verse]
Abraham takes sheep and cattle to give
The two of them make a covenant of peace
He sets apart seven ewe lambs to live
As proof that he dug the well in this place
The place is called Beersheba, they swear
When they had made the covenant at Beersheba
Abimelech and Phicol the commander set out
Returned to the land of the Philistines, true

[Chorus]
Phicol the commander of the army stands
Witness to the oath, the covenant in hands
Seven ewe lambs set apart from the flock
Accept these as my witness that I dug this well

[Verse]
Years pass and Isaac lives in the same land
Abimelech comes again from the city gate
With Ahuzzath the adviser, and Phicol in hand
They saw clearly that the Lord was with you, said they
Isaac asks why they have come to his door
Since they hated him and sent him away from you
They seek a sworn agreement, peace between us
Just as we did you nothing but good and sent you away

[Chorus]
Phicol the commander of the army stands
Witness to the oath, the covenant in hands
Seven ewe lambs set apart from the flock
Accept these as my witness that I dug this well

[Bridge]
He makes them a feast, they eat and drink
Early in the morning they rise and swear
Exchanging oaths with one another, plain
Then Isaac sends them off, they leave him in peace

[Outro]
Phicol the commander of the army stands
Witness to the oath, the covenant in hands
